chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'What is the meaning of the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: Whoever kills a soul, it is as though he killed all the people; and whoever saves a soul, it is as though he saved all the people?'
He (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who extracts it from straying to Guidance, so it is as if he revived it; and the one who extracts it from Guidance to straying, so he has killed it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of killing and reviving souls in Surah Al-Imran verse 32 according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) offers a profound spiritual exegesis of Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:32, redefining 'killing' and 'reviving' the soul as guiding a person from misguidance to guidance and vice versa. This interpretation highlights the concept of *Hayat al-Ruh* (life of the spirit), where spiritual vitality is determined by adherence to divine truth rather than mere physical existence. It underscores the Imam's role in nurturing the faith of the believers, aligning with the Shia emphasis on the transformative power of the Ahl al-Bayt in leading the Ummah.
